title: MODULE 11 — Capstone: Production-Ready Learning Platform API

overview.text: Module objective: Design, build, test, secure, deploy and document a complete backend system by combining all the engineering skills learned throughout the backend development course.
This is not another isolated backend programming exercise.

You will build one complete application that demonstrates your ability to work as a backend engineer: designing architecture, managing data, developing APIs, implementing authentication, handling transactions, optimizing performance, preventing security vulnerabilities, automating testing and operating the application in production.
By the end of this capstone, you should have a working backend application that another developer can understand, test, deploy and maintain.

blocks.text: You will build a Learning Platform Backend API.
The application will provide the backend functionality for an online learning platform where:
Students can register and log in.
Administrators can create and manage courses.
Students can track their learning progress.
The system can send enrollment and learning notifications.
APIs can handle multiple requests efficiently.
Administrators can monitor application health and operations.
The frontend is not the main focus of this capstone. You are building the backend that a web application, mobile application or another authorized client could consume.
Imagine an organization launches a learning platform with:
A student visits the platform and performs the following actions:
Every action communicates with the backend API.
Manages the learning-platform content and operations.
You can add an instructor role as an extension, but the required capstone scope only needs students and administrators. Keep the first implementation focused.
Architecture recommendation: Build this as a modular monolith first, not as 10 separate microservices.
A modular monolith means the application is deployed as one backend service but has clearly separated business modules.
This is appropriate for the capstone because you can demonstrate transactions, security, caching and asynchronous processing without introducing unnecessary distributed-system complexity.
TLS, request routing and traffic controls

It receives requests, validates data, authenticates users, checks permissions and executes business operations.

When 500 students request the same published course description, Redis can serve repeated reads from its cache.

sections.title: 4. Requirement 02 — Role-Based Access for Students and Administrators

blocks.text: The capstone has two required roles:
Administrators manage platform content and authorized administrative operations.
Notice that role authorization alone is insufficient.
For instance, a student should not view another student's progress just because both users share the STUDENT role.
You must implement object ownership checks from Module 09.

@PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')") @PostMapping("/api/v1/admin/courses") public CourseResponse createCourse( @Valid @RequestBody CreateCourseRequest request) { return courseService.createCourse(request); }

@PreAuthorize("hasRole('STUDENT')") @PostMapping("/api/v1/courses/{courseId}/enroll") public EnrollmentResponse enroll( @PathVariable Long courseId, @AuthenticationPrincipal AppUserPrincipal user) { return enrollmentService.enroll( user.getUserId(), courseId ); }
For actual ownership, derive the current user from the authenticated principal rather than allowing the client to choose the student ID.
Completion criteria: Every protected endpoint has a documented permission policy and automated tests for the student and administrator roles.

sections.title: 5. Requirement 03 — Course Creation, Editing and Retrieval

blocks.text: Administrators must be able to create and manage learning content.
The database should store this information in the courses table.
Public or authenticated according to policy
For the initial capstone, a soft-delete or archive operation is generally safer than permanently deleting a course with historical student records.
Do not accept and return database entities directly.
public record CreateCourseRequest( @NotBlank @Size(max = 200) String title, @Size(max = 5000) String description, @NotNull CourseLevel level, @NotBlank String category ) {}
public record CourseResponse( Long id, String title, String description, CourseLevel level, String category, boolean published ) {}
This prevents clients from automatically controlling internal properties such as database IDs, administrative metadata or protected ownership fields.
Check whether it is published or whether the requester has administrative permission.
A course-management API should also have clear rules for draft courses and archived courses.
Completion criteria: Admin can create, update and manage courses. Students can retrieve only courses that the application's access policy permits.

sections.title: 6. Requirement 04 — Student Enrollment and Progress Tracking

blocks.text: This is one of the most important business modules of the capstone.
Enrollment represents the relationship between a student and a course.
Student 201 | v Course 10 — Backend Engineering | v Enrollment 500
The same student can enroll in multiple courses, and each course can have multiple students.
This is a many-to-many relationship represented through an enrollment table.

CREATE TABLE enrollments ( id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, student_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), course_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES courses(id), enrolled_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, status VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ACTIVE', CONSTRAINT unique_student_course UNIQUE (student_id, course_id) );
The unique constraint prevents duplicate student-course enrollment records.
This is important because application-level duplicate checks alone can fail under simultaneous requests.
PostgreSQL supports unique constraints and foreign keys to enforce data integrity at the database level.
The enrollment operation and its associated database changes should execute within an appropriate transaction.

@Service public class EnrollmentService { private final CourseRepository courseRepository; private final EnrollmentRepository enrollmentRepository; public EnrollmentService( CourseRepository courseRepository, EnrollmentRepository enrollmentRepository) { this.courseRepository = courseRepository; this.enrollmentRepository = enrollmentRepository; } @Transactional public Enrollment enroll( Long studentId, Long courseId) { Course course = courseRepository .findByIdAndPublishedTrue(courseId) .orElseThrow(CourseNotFoundException::new); if (enrollmentRepository .existsByStudentIdAndCourseId( studentId, courseId)) { throw new DuplicateEnrollmentException(); } Enrollment enrollment = new Enrollment(studentId, course.getId()); return enrollmentRepository.save(enrollment); } }
The corresponding database uniqueness constraint remains essential because two concurrent requests might both pass the initial existence check.
Catch and translate the resulting database conflict into a consistent API error, taking care that the failed transaction is not reused after a database exception.
Spring's @Transactional provides declarative transaction management, with rollback behaviour that should be understood when defining application exceptions.
An enrollment is only the beginning.
You need to track how much of the course a student completes.
Course: Backend Engineering Module 1: Lesson 1: Completed Lesson 2: Completed Lesson 3: In Progress Module 2: Lesson 1: Not Started Lesson 2: Not Started
The backend should store lesson completion records.

CREATE TABLE lesson_progress ( id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, enrollment_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES enrollments(id), lesson_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES lessons(id), completed BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE, completed_at TIMESTAMPTZ, updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CONSTRAINT unique_enrollment_lesson UNIQUE (enrollment_id, lesson_id) );
You should also validate that the lesson belongs to the course associated with the student's enrollment.
Think carefully about how you calculate progress when courses contain unpublished or archived lessons. Define the denominator consistently.
Completion criteria: Students can enroll without duplicates, mark lessons completed and retrieve accurate course-level progress.

sections.title: 7. Requirement 05 — Database Relationships and Transactional Operations

blocks.text: A learning platform needs multiple related tables.
You should design the database before implementing all the services.
One user can have many enrollments
Conceptual relationship diagram. Notifications and outbox events are separate supporting tables.The relationship structure is:

User 1 -------- N Enrollment Course 1 ------ N Enrollment Course 1 ------ N Module Module 1 ------ N Lesson Enrollment 1 -- N LessonProgress Lesson 1 ------ N LessonProgress User 1 -------- N Notification
A professional database should enforce important business rules.
ALTER TABLE users ADD CONSTRAINT unique_user_email UNIQUE(email);
ALTER TABLE enrollments ADD CONSTRAINT unique_enrollment UNIQUE(student_id, course_id);
ALTER TABLE lesson_progress ADD CONSTRAINT unique_progress UNIQUE(enrollment_id, lesson_id);
Use NOT NULL for properties that must always have values.
Use foreign keys to prevent records from referring to nonexistent parent records.
Create indexes based on actual query patterns.
CREATE INDEX idx_enrollments_student ON enrollments(student_id); CREATE INDEX idx_modules_course ON modules(course_id); CREATE INDEX idx_lessons_module ON lessons(module_id);
Indexes should be supported by query analysis. Avoid adding indexes indiscriminately because they also increase storage and write costs.
Transactions are necessary when multiple database operations must succeed or fail together.
BEGIN TRANSACTION 1. Verify course 2. Create enrollment 3. Create initial progress record, if required 4. Record notification outbox event COMMIT
Suppose enrollment creation succeeds, but recording the required outbox event fails.
The system should not commit a partial operation when both records are part of the same required business transaction.
Use @Transactional around the appropriate service operation.
Completion criteria: The schema has correct relationships and constraints, and related operations cannot leave inconsistent database state.
Imagine the platform has 100,000 courses and learning records.
Should the backend return all 100,000 records in one response?
That could consume excessive memory, increase database workload, create large network responses and slow down the application.
Pagination divides the result set into smaller pages.

@GetMapping public Page<CourseResponse> getCourses( @RequestParam(defaultValue = "0") int page, @RequestParam(defaultValue = "20") int size) { if (page < 0 || size < 1 || size > 100) { throw new IllegalArgumentException( "Invalid pagination parameters" ); } Pageable pageable = PageRequest.of( page, size, Sort.by("createdAt").descending() ); return courseService.getCourses(pageable); }
In an application with user-controlled sorting, validate the requested field against an allowlist.
The response gives the frontend enough information to build pagination controls.
Filtering allows clients to retrieve records matching specific conditions.
The backend should apply the filters to the database query rather than retrieving every course and filtering everything in Java memory.
Spring Data Specifications or a carefully designed custom repository query can support dynamic filtering.
Search allows students to find relevant courses.
For a basic PostgreSQL implementation, you can use indexed queries and PostgreSQL full-text search as the data grows.
8.6 When should you use cursor pagination?
Offset pagination is easy to implement but can become inefficient for very large datasets or frequently changing result sets.
Cursor pagination uses an ordering key to retrieve the next set of records.
This approach can be useful for large, frequently changing feeds, provided that the cursor is based on a stable, indexed ordering.
Completion criteria: Students can retrieve courses through bounded pages, combine filters and search efficiently, and the API validates pagination parameters.

sections.title: 9. Requirement 07 — Redis Caching for Appropriate Read Operations

blocks.text: Caching stores frequently used information in a faster storage system so that the application does not need to repeat expensive database operations unnecessarily.
Course: Backend Engineering Students requesting its details: 500 per minute
First request | v PostgreSQL | v Store course result in Redis Following requests | v Redis | v Return cached course
Redis stores data in memory and can substantially reduce repeated read workload when caching is appropriate.
User-specific progress without a carefully designed access and invalidation strategy.
Frequently changing data with no consistency plan.
PostgreSQL should remain the primary source of truth.
The cache-aside pattern works as follows:
It looks for data in Redis.
9.4 Configure Redis caching in Spring Boot

@Cacheable( cacheNames = "courses", key = "#courseId" ) public CourseResponse getPublishedCourse( Long courseId) { return courseRepository .findPublishedCourse(courseId) .map(courseMapper::toResponse) .orElseThrow(CourseNotFoundException::new); }
When another request uses the same cache key, the cached result can be returned instead of executing the database lookup again.
Spring Data Redis integrates with Spring's cache abstraction, including @Cacheable and RedisCacheManager.
Suppose an administrator updates a course title.
Redis also contains the old result.
If you do not invalidate the cache, students might continue receiving the old title.
Use cache eviction after successful updates.
@CacheEvict( cacheNames = "courses", key = "#courseId" ) @Transactional public void updateCourse( Long courseId, UpdateCourseRequest request) { // Load and update course. }
You must also consider cached course-list pages. Updating one course may require invalidating more than just its individual cache entry.
Use appropriate TTLs and explicit invalidation policies.
Cache by filter and pagination parameters
Do not treat ordinary course cache as an auth store
Invalidate affected course entries and listing entries
Completion criteria: Redis reduces repeat database reads for selected course operations, and updates do not leave stale data indefinitely.
Asynchronous processing means an application can accept a task and allow it to be executed separately from the original HTTP request.
Imagine a student enrolls in a course.
Should the API wait until the email provider finishes?
Email delivery may take several seconds or fail temporarily.
The student should not have to wait for a non-critical email operation before the enrollment is confirmed.
Student | v Enrollment API | +---- Save enrollment | +---- Call email provider | +---- Wait for response | v Return API response
The request waits for the email operation.
Student | v Enrollment API | +---- Save enrollment | +---- Record notification event | v Return enrollment response Background worker | v Process notification | v Send email
This makes user-facing requests less dependent on notification provider availability.
A message broker that allows applications to communicate through queues and message exchanges.
Holds messages that cannot be processed successfully
Enrollment and event committed to PostgreSQL
There is an important design problem that you should understand.

sections.title: 1. Save enrollment in PostgreSQL 2. Publish notification to RabbitMQ

blocks.text: What happens if the enrollment succeeds but RabbitMQ is unavailable?
The enrollment exists, but no notification may be sent.
Reversing the order is also unsafe:
RabbitMQ could receive an event even though the enrollment transaction subsequently fails.
This is known as the dual-write problem.
A reliable solution is the transactional outbox pattern.
Save the enrollment and the notification event inside the same PostgreSQL transaction.

CREATE TABLE outbox_events ( id UUID PRIMARY KEY, event_type VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, aggregate_id BIGINT NOT NULL, payload JSONB NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, published_at TIMESTAMPTZ, attempts INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 );
BEGIN TRANSACTION 1. Insert enrollment 2. Insert outbox event COMMIT
A background publisher later reads pending outbox events and sends them to RabbitMQ.
The publisher should mark an event published only after receiving confirmation from the broker.
RabbitMQ publisher confirms help determine whether the broker accepted a published message, while consumer acknowledgements communicate successful processing.
The notification worker must account for duplicate messages.
A message could be delivered more than once, for example when processing succeeds but acknowledgement is lost.
Every event should have a unique ID.
Consumers should track processed event IDs.
Repeated failures should reach a dead-letter queue.
Do not claim exactly-once email delivery merely because the queue uses acknowledgements. Design for at-least-once delivery and duplicate-safe processing.
Completion criteria: Enrollment remains successful even when an email provider is slow or temporarily unavailable, and the notification is retried or tracked for recovery.
11. Requirement 09 — Input Validation and Standardized Error Responses
Every API request should be treated as untrusted.
The backend must reject invalid data before it reaches sensitive business logic or the database.
Validation should happen at multiple levels:
public record RegisterRequest( @NotBlank @Size(max = 100) String name, @NotBlank @Email String email, @NotBlank @Size(min = 12, max = 128) String password ) {}

@PostMapping("/register") public ResponseEntity<UserResponse> register( @Valid @RequestBody RegisterRequest request) { UserResponse response = authService.register(request); return ResponseEntity.status(201).body(response); }
The application validates the request before executing registration logic.
A production password policy should also consider breached-password screening, secure recovery, rate limiting and usability.
Some conditions cannot be verified using simple annotations.
A course must exist before enrollment.
An archived course cannot receive new enrollments.
A lesson must belong to the enrolled course.
A user cannot modify another user's progress.
These rules belong in the appropriate business services and database constraints.
A common mistake is returning a different error format from every controller.
This makes frontend development and API consumption difficult.
Instead, define a consistent error-response structure.

{ "type": "https://api.example.com/problems/validation-error", "title": "Validation failed", "status": 400, "detail": "One or more fields are invalid.", "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "instance": "/api/v1/auth/register", "fieldErrors": { "email": "Must be a valid email address" }, "traceId": "trace-abc123" }
This example follows the general structure of HTTP Problem Details, with application-specific extension fields.
Spring Framework provides ProblemDetail support for standardized HTTP API errors.
Use @RestControllerAdvice rather than duplicating exception handling across controllers.

@RestControllerAdvice public class GlobalExceptionHandler { @ExceptionHandler(CourseNotFoundException.class) public ResponseEntity<ProblemDetail> handleNotFound( CourseNotFoundException exception) { ProblemDetail problem = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail( HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "The requested course does not exist." ); problem.setTitle("Course not found"); problem.setProperty("code", "COURSE_NOT_FOUND"); return ResponseEntity .status(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND) .body(problem); } }
A complete implementation should also handle:
Never expose stack traces, SQL statements or credentials in client-facing errors.
Semantically invalid request, where used by the API contract
Completion criteria: Every API error follows the agreed response format and returns an appropriate status code without leaking internal implementation details.
12. Requirement 10 — API Security and Rate Limiting
Your final application must combine the lessons from Module 09.
Follow the OWASP API Security risks as an additional review checklist, especially object authorization, function authorization, resource consumption and security configuration.
Rate limiting controls how frequently a client can access an API.
Imagine a public login endpoint receives:
Without limits, attackers may repeatedly attempt logins or consume backend resources.
Rate limiting can restrict excessive requests.
These are sample policies for the capstone, not universal security thresholds.
5 per hour per trusted client identity
You should account for distributed abuse rather than relying entirely on the client IP.
For login, rate limits may combine account identifier, source address and other risk signals.
Be careful when interpreting forwarded IP headers: trust them only when set by known, controlled proxies.
12.4 Why use Redis for rate limiting?
Suppose your application has three backend instances.
If each instance maintains its own in-memory rate counter, the overall limit may be inconsistent.
Redis can provide shared rate-limit state across instances.
All backend instances | v Shared Redis rate-limit storage | v Consistent counters
Use an atomic operation or suitable distributed rate-limiting algorithm, such as token bucket or sliding window.
Anonymous users cannot access protected endpoints.
Users cannot access another student's records.
Protected entity properties cannot be changed through requests.
Expired and invalid tokens are rejected.
Invalid database input does not manipulate queries.
Rate limits apply across backend instances.
Sensitive information does not appear in responses or logs.
Completion criteria: The backend enforces permissions independently of the frontend and applies resource-protection controls to important public and authenticated endpoints.

sections.title: 16. Requirement 14 — Logging, Health Checks and Monitoring

blocks.text: 16.1 What does observability mean in this project?
After deploying the application, you need to understand how it behaves.
Notification messages are accumulating in a queue.
The course listing API returns errors.
A worker repeatedly fails to send notifications.
You should be able to detect and investigate these problems.
Use the three core observability signals:
These endpoints should provide information about application health without exposing unnecessary internal details.

Spring Boot Actuator uses Micrometer to expose and export application metrics, including HTTP, JVM, data source and cache measurements. It supports Prometheus integration through /actuator/prometheus when configured.
Your final monitoring dashboard should contain:
Illustrative request traffic during a sample monitoring window.
Illustrative dashboard, not a live backend connection or actual application performance report.
Your application should log important operations such as:
Avoid sensitive credentials and access tokens.
Pending messages exceed an agreed threshold
Sustained memory usage approaches the limit
Thresholds should be calibrated using load-test results and actual production behaviour.
Completion criteria: You can see application health, identify performance bottlenecks and detect important operational failures through logs, metrics, traces and alerts.

22. Technical Architecture Report — What Must You Explain?
Your architecture report is especially important because it demonstrates that you understand the reasons behind your implementation.
What problem does the platform solve?
Why Java, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, Redis and RabbitMQ?
Why were these tables and relationships selected?
What information is cached and how is it invalidated?
How are notification events delivered reliably?
How is the backend packaged and released?
How are problems detected and investigated?
What does the system not yet support?
"Why did you use PostgreSQL instead of storing all application information in Redis?"

PostgreSQL is the primary persistent relational database. It provides relationships, constraints and transactional operations suitable for users, courses, enrollments and progress. Redis is used selectively to accelerate repeat reads and maintain shared rate-limiting state. Redis is not the authoritative database for learning records.
That is the sort of engineering reasoning your architecture report should demonstrate.
Your final project can be evaluated using the following structure.
During the final demonstration, you should be able to perform this complete workflow:
Authenticate and receive an access token.
Retrieve course details from Redis on repeated requests.
Verify the asynchronous notification is processed.
Verify that the Redis cache is invalidated correctly.
Verify that students cannot perform administrative operations.
Build and run the Docker containers.
Inspect structured logs and request traces.
Simulate a failure and demonstrate recovery.

sections.title: 25. How the Entire Backend Course Comes Together

blocks.text: The capstone combines all the engineering concepts learned throughout the backend course.
Classes, interfaces, abstraction and application design
PostgreSQL, entity relationships, indexes and transactions
HTTP methods, endpoints and response design
BOLA, BFLA, injection prevention and rate limiting
Logs, metrics, traces and incident investigation
The difference is that earlier modules taught each concept separately. The capstone makes you combine them into one functioning system.
What makes this a professional-level capstone?
Design a complete backend with clear architecture, business logic and database relationships.
Protect authentication, authorization, private information and application resources.
Use database indexing, caching, pagination and asynchronous processing appropriately.
Write automated tests that verify business behaviour, database consistency, security and integrations.
Package the application, deploy containers and configure production environments.
Monitor performance, investigate failures and maintain the application in production.
The central engineering principle of Module 11:

A production-ready learning platform is not simply a collection of API endpoints. It is a complete software system in which authentication, authorization, business logic, database consistency, caching, asynchronous processing, automated testing, deployment and observability work together.
Your final objective is to deliver an application that another engineer can run, understand, test, deploy and maintain—not merely a project that works on your own computer.
This capstone is the final demonstration that you can take backend engineering concepts and turn them into a complete, production-oriented application.
